authority: product owner — consumer B, build this
purpose: Close product-owned choices that would otherwise become week-one implementation forks while keeping the V10/retention choice fail-closed until its architecture input exists.
scope: NEXT OpenSIP CLI first implementation milestone in docs/coop/v1-slice.md

P-1.rule: Preserve a future-safe contribution boundary, but do not build a marketplace, public lifecycle parity, extension discovery service, or ecosystem governance depth for v1.
P-1.doesNotMean: The internal boundary may be vendor-coupled or that untrusted code is admitted.

P-2.rule: Contributions are narrow producers or data-only rules/profiles. They never own root commands, policy, persistence, rendering, termination, or host lifecycle.
P-2.milestoneRequirement: The first vertical slice requires bundled algorithms, bundled TypeScript/Rust providers, and bundled declarative rules only; external distribution/lifecycle is not an exit gate.

A1-RI-04.rule: The CI/non-interactive profile does not load or resolve layer-4 analysis-affecting untracked overrides. Their presence is not an admission failure. Local interactive runs may use layer 4 only when its values and provenance enter PlanId and the explain projection.
A1-RI-04.why: This prevents an unreviewed local file from changing CI without turning mere file presence into a CI denial-of-service switch.

VER-PIVOT-COST.rule: A detector pivot runs only when a detector major changes and a baseline/gate comparison is explicitly requested. Ordinary analysis never invokes it. An unavailable pivot is INDETERMINATE, never attributed to code.
VER-PIVOT-COST.milestoneRequirement: Optional for the first vertical-slice exit.
VER-PIVOT-COST.evidencePosture: Affordability remains UNMEASURED; no cheap/free claim is authorized.

PUBLIC-RULE-IR.rule: The rule IR may be an internal versioned implementation contract, but v1 makes no public compatibility promise for third-party rule authors.
PUBLIC-RULE-IR.revisitWhen: P-1 changes to an explicit ecosystem-depth commitment.

SUPPORT-WINDOWS.rule: The VERSIONING support-window counts remain usable architecture defaults only when consumer-facing material labels them provisional/GUESSED. They are not SLAs and their empirical correctness is not an architecture-freeze blocker.
SUPPORT-WINDOWS.evidencePosture: NOT DISCHARGED until real adoption and compatibility evidence exists.

G3-SUBSTRATE.rule: Rust host/core, bundled TypeScript provider, bundled exactly pinned rustc_driver sidecar, full default install profile, finite supported-platform matrix, and offline assets are the v1 substrate defaults.
G3-SUBSTRATE.evidencePosture: Architecture binding does not qualify or demonstrate the release lanes.

CD-RT-5.question: Accept or replace the V10/retention architecture candidate's default durable-custody posture, including whether any durable retention is implicit.
CD-RT-5.ruleWhilePending: No implementer may choose a retention default and no freeze may claim V10 resolved.
CD-RT-5.unblocksWhen: Phase 1A supplies an independently reviewed evaluation-proof, verification/regeneration closure, degradation model, and purge semantics.

invariants: PD-1: Every non-retention Phase-2 row has one choice, not a menu.
PD-2: A product choice may narrow initial scope but may not weaken a binding identity, evidence, threat, admission, or termination contract.
PD-3: Excluded authority is rejected at admission; a future-safe boundary is not permission to ship its dependents.
PD-4: Architecture defaults and release demonstrations remain separate states.
PD-5: The retention row remains visibly blocked until Phase 1A supplies the missing architecture input.
knownLimitations: CD-RT-5 is intentionally unresolved because its required Phase-1A input is in flight.
This artifact chooses product posture; it does not demonstrate product behavior.
A later scope expansion requires an explicit product disposition and any mechanism named by the affected binding contract.
